verdict: REVISE, but a materially weaker REVISE than Q016's, and the pre-registration did not cleanly anticipate the outcome shape (stated plainly, not smoothed). Q018 tested the one remaining untested mitigation for Q016's Round 2 file-lock failure: replace Assembly.LoadFrom (which holds a Windows file-lock on Satellite.dll for the process lifetime) with a collectible AssemblyLoadContext that can be unloaded before the builder overwrites the DLL. Three staged rounds. ROUND A (isolated OS-level claim, no type provider): PASS, with a load-bearing caveat -- a collectible ALC releases the lock, but ONLY with <TieredCompilation>false</TieredCompilation>. With default tiered JIT the ALC deterministically failed to collect 3/3 (~1930ms of forced-GC pressure) due to Tier-0 quick-JIT's imprecise GC liveness reporting; with tiering off it collected on the first iteration (~57ms) 3/3. TieredCompilation defaults ON in every real host (Ionide/FSAC/dotnet build/MSBuild), which Myriad does not control. ROUND B (fact-finding): the design's own prediction was WRONG -- a process-wide constructor counter shows FCS constructs a FRESH SatelliteProvider instance per checker.Compile() call, not the same instance persisting across Invalidate(). So sourceAssemblies staleness (a construction-time concern) is not the blocker; the blocker is old-instance retention. ROUND C (the actual mitigation): FAIL, and not in either pre-registered shape. Even an ideal externally-triggered eviction (Q018Hooks.evictAndForceCollect, using Round A's proven technique, called BEFORE the write, deliberately sidestepping the FileSystemWatcher chicken-and-egg problem -- a change-triggered watcher cannot release a lock that blocks the very change it waits for) reported released=false after 30 iterations; the overwrite hit the SAME 'Could not open file for writing' lock exception; the freshly-constructed instance #2 correctly resolved stale v1 (Create rejects 3 args, GetEmail absent). This review reproduced all three rounds independently (tooling worked, unlike Q016's reviewer; scratch build diffed byte-identical to checked-in artifacts) and ran three experiments beyond reproduction. (1) FRESH-CHECKER (the executor's own named 'single most informative' untested follow-up): a local checker1 compiles pre-regen, then InvalidateAll + ClearLanguageServiceRootCaches + drop the reference + forced GC + evict, then a fresh checker2 for post-regen. Result: STILL LOCKED (released=false, lock exception, stale v1). The constructor counter increments across the two SEPARATE checkers (instance #1 under checker1, #2 under checker2), and a load-context census shows Satellite still present in its collectible ALC after checker-drop + GC -- proving the retained reference is PROCESS-GLOBAL in FCS's type-provider hosting, not checker-instance-scoped. The executor's most hopeful escape ('a real host that doesn't hold one checker forever would fix it') is empirically dead within FSharpChecker-as-library. (2) FCS-READER ISOLATION (a hypothesis the executor never raised): compile a consumer that references Satellite.dll directly and uses a type from it with NO type provider at all -- Satellite loads into no managed ALC, same-process write-open succeeds, subprocess overwrite succeeds (exit=0). So FCS's own -r referenced-assembly reader does NOT lock the file; the lock genuinely comes from the provider's collectible ALC, confirming the executor aimed at the right culprit and ruling out the one alternative that would have made the mitigation misdirected. (3) AGGRESSIVE-OPTIMIZATION (the executor's named untested press-on #3): [<MethodImpl(AggressiveOptimization)>] on the load/probe methods under default tiered JIT still FAILED 3/3 (collected=false, 30 iterations) -- forcing just the provider's own methods to full-tier JIT does not restore precise-enough GC liveness; only disabling tiering process-wide does. So there is NO demonstrated library-controllable escape from the Round A caveat either. Verdict reasoning against the literal thresholds: KILL is OUT because its sole trigger ('the isolated ALC-unload test itself fails, even with no other live references') did not fire -- Round A releases the lock on iteration 1 when references are genuinely gone; calling this KILL would assert collectible ALCs cannot release file locks, which Round A disproves. SHIP/NULL are out on substance (Round C failed outright). REVISE is the least-wrong label -- piece 1 (foundational OS mechanism) confirmed, piece 3 (full integration) fails -- chosen because KILL's own narrow definition rules itself out, NOT because the outcome matches REVISE's optimism. The only divergence from the registered REVISE text is the failure SHAPE: the same file-lock exception recurs (because the reference is process-global) rather than the predicted NEW source/target identity mismatch. What travels with this REVISE and matters more than the label: the specific collectible-ALC mitigation is EXHAUSTED in-process (not merely unproven) -- it was the one candidate Q016's review named for Round 2, it fails under the most favorable possible conditions, and the fresh-checker fallback fails too, so there is no demonstrated in-process fix for Round 2's lock; the blocker is bounded by elimination to FCS process-global retention of the provider's ALC-loaded satellite assembly (not the provider's own cache, not FCS's -r reader, not the checker instance), though the exact FCS structure was not traced; and this tightens Q016 objection 3's conclusion further -- the cross-project satellite-DLL TP's sole differentiator over an ordinary <ProjectReference> (live re-exposure via Invalidate()) now has no working in-process implementation on Windows, so the honest guidance should drop its conditional ('use a ProjectReference; the ALC-unload path does not work'). Top follow-ups, prioritized: (1) an out-of-process design-time host is the only in-principle escape the hypothesis did not already scope out (a separate process's ALC is torn down on exit, sidestepping the process-global retention), but it is a large lift that may not beat a plain ProjectReference -- the honest alternative is to stop pursuing live re-exposure for the cross-project case and record that in BACKLOG item 15; (2) name the exact FCS retaining structure from source before spending on (1), to confirm whether any in-process release is theoretically possible; (3) treat the TieredCompilation/JIT-liveness requirement as a hard host-environment constraint, not a tunable, since AggressiveOptimization is ruled out; (4) real-IDE-host test (standing caveat since Q006, lower priority since aggressive in-process recycling already does not help).
